decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-074 scopes what a named audience (a dataroom group) can see, with separate view and download flags per document and per folder. The specification names four linked records and two ACL scopes with different write semantics. Which backend shape should the domain package use?

state.problem: WF-074 scopes what a named audience (a dataroom group) can see, with separate view and download flags per document and per folder. The specification names four linked records and two ACL scopes with different write semantics. Which backend shape should the domain package use?

candidate_solutions.new_domain_package_audience_permissions: Create backend/dsr/audience_permissions/ with vocabulary, rules, inferences and engine. Reads the room's own document rows from the 'document' and 'documentFolder' collections that already exist on main rather than copying them. Owns the four group collections and the per-item ACL itself.
candidate_solutions.extend_security_governance: Add the module to the existing dsr/security_governance package, because the specification names security-governance as the domain.
candidate_solutions.reuse_link_gating_for_both_scopes: Put group permissions and link permissions in the existing dsr/link_gating package, because a group link is still a link.

context.sources_of_item_ids: The specification's data sources name 'DataroomDocument join rows (ddoc_...) and data room folder rows as the item_id targets'. This repository already owns those rows: dsr/library.py defines DOCUMENT_COLLECTION='document' and FOLDER_COLLECTION='documentFolder', and dsr/documents.py owns COLLECTION='document'. WF-003 built them.
context.existing_packages_checked: backend/dsr contains security_governance, link_gating, roles, permissions, access_controls, revocation, identity_verification and others. None of them models a named audience with a per-item view and download ACL. security_governance holds WF-075 engagement review modules; link_gating holds WF-069 password and WF-070 NDA link gates. Neither names a group or a per-item permission set.
context.collision_risk: WF-004 owns buyer roles and access expiry. WF-014 and WF-069 own link access windows and password gates. This workflow is the per-item layer above them and must not rewrite their rows.
context.mandate_from_task_file: TASK.md says: if a package for the domain already exists under backend/dsr/, extend it, do not create a second one for the same domain. It then lists the packages this agent may extend: crm_integration, throttle, lead_score, visitor_identification, lead_qualification, round_robin, concierge_router. The audience-permissions domain is not in that list.
